fields.Front: What are the core functional requirements to clarify for a Music Streaming Service OOD interview?
fields.Back: 1) Browse/search a catalog of songs, albums, artists. 2) Play/pause/skip/seek playback. 3) Create, edit, and share playlists. 4) Follow artists and see a personalized feed. 5) Get song recommendations. 6) Support tiered subscriptions (free vs premium) affecting available features.

fields.Front: What should you explicitly mark out of scope when designing a Music Streaming Service in an interview?
fields.Back: The actual audio codec/streaming protocol (e.g. adaptive bitrate), DRM/licensing enforcement details, and the ML internals of a recommendation model — treat recommendation as a pluggable strategy interface instead of designing the model.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the User class?
fields.Back: Holds account/profile data, subscription tier, owned playlists, followed artists, and listening history — used as input to recommendations and to enforce feature gating (e.g. skip limits on the free tier).

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the Playlist class?
fields.Back: An ordered collection of songs with a name, an owner, and optional collaborators; supports add/remove/reorder operations and knows nothing about how it is played back.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the Player (playback engine) class?
fields.Back: Manages the current play queue and playback position: play(), pause(), skip(), seek(); tracks the current PlaybackState and notifies observers when the now-playing song changes.

Aggregation, not composition: a Playlist references existing Song objects (often via a PlaylistEntry wrapper that also stores position/order and who added it) — deleting a playlist must not delete the underlying songs.
One-to-many ownership: a User owns zero or more Playlists. For collaborative playlists, a playlist instead holds a set of contributor Users in addition to a single owner.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits song recommendations, and why?
fields.Back: Strategy. RecommendationEngine holds a RecommendationStrategy interface (e.g. genre-based, collaborative-filtering, recently-played-based); the concrete algorithm is swapped at runtime per user/experiment without changing the engine's calling code.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits the now-playing / live activity feature, and why?
fields.Back: Observer. The Player (or a dedicated NowPlayingSubject) notifies registered listeners — a friend-activity feed, a lock-screen widget, analytics — whenever the current song changes, decoupling playback from every consumer of that event.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits playlist creation, and why?
fields.Back: Factory. A PlaylistFactory centralizes construction of different playlist variants (plain user playlist, collaborative playlist, auto-generated smart mix) so client code calls one createPlaylist(type, owner, name) instead of knowing every concrete subclass.

fields.Front: What is the shape of RecommendationEngine's public API, given it uses the Strategy pattern?
fields.Back: getRecommendations(User user, int limit) delegates to strategy.recommend(user, library, limit); a setStrategy(RecommendationStrategy) method lets the engine swap algorithms at runtime (e.g. A/B testing).

fields.Front: What four methods form the core playback API on Player?
fields.Back: play(), pause(), skip(), and seek(position) — each updates PlaybackState and, on a song change, notifies now-playing observers.

fields.Front: Edge case: a song is removed from the catalog (rights expired) while it still appears in thousands of user playlists. How should the design handle this?
fields.Back: Soft-delete/tombstone the Song rather than hard-deleting it: mark it unavailable, keep the object (and its id) so playlists don't break, and have the Player skip unavailable songs during playback with a UI indicator instead of a crash.

fields.Front: Edge case: the same account starts playback on a phone and then on a web browser. What should happen?
fields.Back: Enforce a single active playback session per account (common for personal tiers): starting playback on the new device sends a stop/transfer signal to the previous device's Player instance, so only one device is ever actually streaming at a time.

fields.Front: (Java) Implement the RecommendationStrategy interface and a GenreBasedStrategy concrete implementation.
fields.Back:
public interface RecommendationStrategy {
    List<Song> recommend(User user, MusicLibrary library, int limit);
}

public class GenreBasedStrategy implements RecommendationStrategy {
    @Override
    public List<Song> recommend(User user, MusicLibrary library, int limit) {
        Set<String> favoriteGenres = user.getTopGenres();
        return library.getAllSongs().stream()
            .filter(song -> favoriteGenres.contains(song.getGenre()))
            .filter(song -> !user.hasPlayed(song))
            .limit(limit)
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }
}

fields.Front: (Python) Implement an Observer-pattern NowPlayingSubject that a FriendActivityFeed listener can subscribe to.
fields.Back:
class NowPlayingSubject:
    def __init__(self):
        self._observers = []
        self._current_song = None

    def attach(self, observer):
        self._observers.append(observer)

    def detach(self, observer):
        self._observers.remove(observer)

    def set_current_song(self, song):
        self._current_song = song
        self._notify()

    def _notify(self):
        for observer in self._observers:
            observer.on_now_playing_changed(self._current_song)


class FriendActivityFeed:
    def on_now_playing_changed(self, song):
        print(f"Now playing: {song.title} by {song.artist}")

fields.Front: (Java) Implement a PlaylistFactory that builds different playlist variants from a PlaylistType enum.
fields.Back:
public class PlaylistFactory {
    public static Playlist createPlaylist(PlaylistType type, User owner, String name) {
        switch (type) {
            case USER_CREATED:
                return new Playlist(name, owner, false);
            case COLLABORATIVE:
                return new CollaborativePlaylist(name, owner);
            case AUTO_GENERATED_MIX:
                return new SmartMixPlaylist(name, owner);
            default:
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown playlist type: " + type);
        }
    }
}

fields.Front: (Python) Implement Player.play(), pause(), and skip() against a play queue.
fields.Back:
class Player:
    def __init__(self, queue):
        self.queue = queue
        self.state = PlaybackState.STOPPED
        self.current_index = 0

    def play(self):
        if not self.queue:
            return
        self.state = PlaybackState.PLAYING

    def pause(self):
        if self.state == PlaybackState.PLAYING:
            self.state = PlaybackState.PAUSED

    def skip(self):
        self.current_index = (self.current_index + 1) % len(self.queue)
        self.play()

fields.Text: The core classes in a Music Streaming Service design are {{c1::User}}, {{c2::Song}} (with Album/Artist metadata), {{c3::Playlist}}, {{c4::Player}} (playback engine), {{c5::MusicLibrary}} (catalog/search), and {{c6::RecommendationEngine}}.
The PlaybackState enum for the player is {{c1::PLAYING}}, {{c2::PAUSED}}, and {{c3::STOPPED}}.
